message:
feat: bring the remote-execution surface to parity with the Go SDK

The client could launch a run, poll it, and hand back raw literals. This
fills in the rest of the surface the Go SDK exposes for driving tasks that
are already deployed, and hardens the transport underneath it.

Task and run surface:
- getTask() returns TaskDetails with the resolved version, typed interface,
  and registered default inputs.
- Inputs are validated locally before anything is sent: unknown names and
  missing required inputs fail fast, and omitted inputs fall back to the
  task's registered defaults.
- outputs() returns plain JavaScript values keyed by output name; rawData()
  still exposes the wire-format literals.
- All 15 Go run options: labels, annotations, env vars, interruptible,
  cache overwrite, queue, action concurrency, raw-data path, run base dir,
  service account, run relations, and recovery with force-rerun.

Progress and drill-down:
- run.watch() is an async iterator over WatchActionDetails that reconnects
  through idle timeouts and rollouts, and falls back to polling when a
  transport rejects server streaming.
- ActionHandle lists and inspects the actions a run is made of, including
  per-attempt records and error/abort/signal info.
- ConditionHandle.signal() resumes a paused task, choosing the payload type
  from the condition's declared type.

Connecting:
- initFromConfig() reads flytectl/uctl-style YAML using the same search
  order as the Go and Python SDKs; initFromApiKey() mirrors its Go
  counterpart.
- Interactive logins for Node — PKCE, device flow, and external token
  commands — with OAuth discovery and a 0600 file token cache.
- project and domain can be client defaults, overridden per call.

Transport hardening:
- Unary calls retry on Unavailable with linear backoff, and each attempt is
  bounded by a deadline. Bulk data transfers are exempt from the deadline,
  since their duration scales with payload size.
- A request answered with Unauthenticated drops the cached token and retries
  once, recovering from tokens revoked or rotated server-side.
- Private-CA and proxy support: caCertFilePath, insecureSkipVerify, and
  proxyCommand. TLS settings reach discovery and token requests too, not
  just the RPCs.
- An org interceptor fills empty org fields on outgoing messages, so the raw
  services.* clients work without threading org through by hand.

Correctness fixes:
- RECOVERED is terminal and counts as success, matching the IDL.
- org is optional: single-tenant deployments and IP-addressed endpoints have
  none, and deriving one from IP octets was wrong.
- A required input passed as null is now rejected instead of silently
  dropped from the request.

Tooling and docs:
- buf.build/flyteorg/flyte no longer exists, so `pnpm gen` now generates
  from a flyteorg/flyte checkout. Regenerating also picked up
  ACTION_PHASE_RECOVERED, which the committed types predated.
- 279 unit tests, plus an opt-in end-to-end suite that runs real tasks
  against a live control plane (see test/e2e/README.md).
- README gains a quickstart verified end to end against a deployed task.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
